idiom_name: self-referential step methods plus a single terminal operation
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: choose the chain root and give it one method per DSL step, named in the domain's vocabulary; every step performs its part and returns the context for the next call - the same receiver when the chain mutates one object, the next stage or a fresh value when the chain is immutable. Provide exactly one terminal operation that consumes the accumulated state (build/execute/toList) and put cross-step validation there. Decide consciously what replaces a per-step error signal: exceptions, a terminal validation step, or a result carried to the terminal. Keep the fluent verbs on a dedicated expression builder when the underlying API must stay command-query, and fix the receiver type (self type, this.type, CRTP, covariant returns) for subclasses.
code_sketch:
client = http.client().timeout(10).retries(3).on_error(log).build()

# step (mutable)      def timeout(self, t): self._t = t; return self
# step (immutable)    def timeout(self, t): return replace(self, _t=t)
# terminal            def build(self): validate(self); return HttpClient(self._t, ...)
pitfalls: Mixing mutable self-returning steps with immutable value-returning steps in one API: callers cannot tell whether a link changed the previous object or produced a new one, and reuse of the chain silently aliases state.
No per-step error channel: a chain whose steps can fail must defer, throw or smuggle the failure, so the failure mode must be designed and documented with the grammar, not left to callers.
Chaining through other objects' getters (a.b().c().d()) is navigation, not fluency: it breaks information hiding and turns one API change into a long chain edit.

Creating invalid intermediate states: allowing the chain to proceed without required fields (e.g., building a request without a URL) until the terminal build() call - callers get cryptic errors at the end rather than fail-fast at the point of omission.
Breaking IDE discoverability by returning generic Object or Any from step methods, losing the type-guided autocomplete that is the primary benefit of fluent interfaces in statically typed languages.

Wrong move: chaining every method that happens to return an object (customer.getAddress().getCity().getName()) -> the call site is fragile to every internal restructuring and encapsulation is broken -> instead design a grammar: steps on one abstraction in domain vocabulary, navigation replaced by a step that asks for what the caller needs (Fowler: fluency is not method chaining).

Wrong move: putting fluent with*/set* verbs directly on the domain entity to avoid writing a separate builder -> the entity's API violates command-query separation, mocks and diffs become unreadable, and DSL-only verbs pollute the domain model -> instead isolate the fluent surface in a separate expression-builder object that translates each step into ordinary command-query calls on the subject.

Wrong move: letting chains continue past a terminal or assertion-returning method (isEqualTo(...) followed by more steps) -> the grammar has no end, callers chain past the point where intent is complete and failure messages mislead (documented in the JsonUnit API post-mortem) -> instead make the terminal return a final, non-chainable type (or void) so the grammar ends at compile time.
